URL: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202611186347
Iran International, published 18 November 2026

According to the report, Iran has targeted US Navy vessels, military facilities and commercial tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, while American forces have intercepted incoming drones and missiles and occasionally struck missile launchers and other targets inside Iran.

Most of the US strikes have not been publicly disclosed, particularly over the past two months, the officials said.

“They are carrying out these strikes and not acknowledging them,” a person familiar with the matter told NBC News.

The report said US fighter jets struck an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site Tuesday following a drone attack targeting a US radar system in Bahrain. Iran claimed the drones hit the radar, but US Central Command said they were intercepted without damage or injuries.

NBC News reported that the continuing conflict was costing the United States millions of dollars daily, with more than 50,000 American troops and two aircraft carrier strike groups deployed in the Middle East.

The Pentagon declined to comment, while the White House did not respond to NBC News' request for comment.

"])•••$RC("B:4","S:4")More StoriesHow Thai clerics in Iran were recruited to attack Israeli embassy in BangkokNov 17, 2026, 22:13 GMT+0•Mojtaba PourmohsenListen to this article100%Lebanon’s Hezbollah, acting under the IRGC Quds Force’s direction, recruited six Thai clerics who had studied in Qom for a plot to attack the Israeli embassy in Bangkok, a Western intelligence source and a source close to the Quds Force told Iran International.

The sources identified the six men as recruits of Unit 910, the overseas operations unit of the Iran-backed Lebanese group. They said the plot was thwarted.

One member of the network said a Lebanese man he knew as Abu Hassan was his direct handler and supplied him with information for the planned attack.

The two sources identified Abu Hassan as Majed Abdullah, also known as Fadi Kassab, and said he began recruiting students at Al-Mustafa International University in Qom around 2020 with help from the Quds Force.

Kassab’s earlier mission in Bangkok

Kassab’s involvement in Thailand dated back to at least 2012, the sources said. That year, he entered the country under an assumed name to plan and oversee attacks on Israeli interests in Bangkok. The sources identified Hussein Atris, a Swedish-Lebanese national arrested at Bangkok airport that year, as one of his operatives.

100%Atris led Thai police to a warehouse outside the capital where bomb-making materials had been stored. A Thai court convicted him the following year of illegally possessing the materials.

The two sources said Kassab prepared recruits for Unit 910 and had also been linked to operations in Cyprus, Bulgaria, the United States and Canada. They described a division of responsibilities in Iran. A Lebanese national named Mohammad Hassan oversaw Hezbollah’s operations in the country and trained recruits, while Kassab planned attacks on Israeli interests.

100%From Qom’s seminaries to Bangkok

At the center of the Thai network, the sources said, was Mubarak Hosseini, a cleric who had spent more than three decades in Iran and later became head of Al-Mustafa’s alumni association.

100%His family’s ties to Iran went back to 1985, when his cousin Salman Hosseini, a Shia cleric, came to the country and was recruited by the Hojjatieh Association, the sources said. Salman subsequently made regular trips to Thailand to recruit others, including Mubarak.

In a 2023 interview with the Iranian publication Ofogh-e Howzeh, Mubarak said he arrived in Iran in 1991 and studied first at Qom’s seminary, then at the International Centre for Islamic Studies. He later pursued a doctorate in political science at Al-Mustafa, which was founded in 2008 on the orders of then-Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

100%The US Treasury sanctioned the university in 2020, saying the Quds Force used it to recruit for intelligence work and overseas operations.

Mubarak went on to head the Association of Thai Clerics and manage the Thai-language website of Khamenei’s office. In Bangkok, he established the Ahl al-Bayt religious center and founded an association called Supporters of Velayat-e Faqih, a reference to the doctrine of clerical rule underpinning the Islamic Republic.

100%Speaking to Iranian state television, Mubarak said he founded the association to “express affection for the Supreme Leader and the leader of Muslims” and to “prevent British and American Shiites from gaining influence in Thailand, in accordance with the Supreme Leader’s instructions.”

Mubarak and Salman helped Hezbollah recruit five other men from among Al-Mustafa’s students, the two sources said. Four of the five had family ties to Mubarak or to one of the other recruits.

The sources identified two of Mubarak’s sons-in-law, Mohammad Koim Akbar Syed and Seyyed Abbas Sadarsan, as members of the network. A third recruit, Ismail Pathan, was Mohammad Koim’s brother-in-law. Pathan graduated from Al-Mustafa and is active in the Ahl al-Bayt World Assembly, an Iranian religious organization that operates under the supreme leader’s supervision.

100%The fourth was Mubarak’s nephew, Ahmad Hossein Prathansakul, also an Al-Mustafa graduate, the sources said.

100%100%The sources identified Syedaree Sakkitticha as the only one of the six with no fa

mily connection to the others. They said he organized anti-Israel demonstrations in Bangkok. In 2023, Sakkitticha accompanied Meysam Motiei, an Iranian religious chanter associated with Khamenei’s office, during a visit to Thailand.

100%Quds Force source names three financial backers

The source close to the Quds Force identified three Iranian institutions affiliated with the supreme leader as financial backers of the network. They were Al-Mustafa International University, the Ahl al-Bayt World Assembly and Astan Quds Razavi, a wealthy Iranian religious foundation with extensive business holdings. The source said the World Assembly helped raise money for the network through seminars.

Motiei spoke publicly about financial support for Thai Shiites after his 2023 trip. He told Iranian state television that he and his companions had received no payment for the visit and had taken money with them for Thai Shiites he described as facing severe hardship. Motiei said Khamenei had encouraged him to spend as much as possible on the young people he met.

Mubarak also has business interests in Iran. He serves on the boards of Mobin Masir Mandegar Apadana and Pishtaz Sanat Mobin Pars, both of which trade in oil and petrochemical products.

After the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Mubarak addressed rising oil prices in a Facebook post aimed at Thais. He told them Thailand’s Energy Ministry was not responsible, blamed the United States and Israel, and urged people to demonstrate outside their embassies in Bangkok.

On April 26, Mubarak was seen at a nighttime rally in Qom in support of Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father as supreme leader.

100%US strikes Qeshm Island after Iran drone attack on American base in BahrainNov 17, 2026, 17:29 GMT+0Listen to this article100%Smoke rises on Iran's Qeshm Island after airstrikes attributed to the US military on Nov. 17, 2026.US fighter jets struck a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Tuesday after Iranian drones targeted Bahrain, in an exchange that threatened efforts to ease the conflict.

A US military official said American aircraft used precision munitions to hit the site, describing the strike as an act of self-defense.

“The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets,” the official said. “US Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region.”

Iranian provincial official Ahmad Nafisi said the attack on Qeshm caused no damage to residential or commercial areas or vital infrastructure.

Iranian media reported that US forces had hit an air defense missile launcher in the island’s Nariman area. The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency reported that several projectiles had struck the island.

The strike came hours after the Guards said they had targeted a US radar system at Bahrain’s Isa Air Base in response to what they described as continued violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones.

The US military said the Iranian drones had been intercepted without damaging American equipment or injuring US personnel.

“Multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel,” US Central Command said on X, adding that US and partner forces remained highly vigilant.

Iran’s army separately said it had shot down a LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz using domestically developed air defenses. The US has not commented on the army’s claim.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed the Iranian attacks with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry said. Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington’s commitment to Bahrain’s security and that of its regional partners.

Saudi Arabia called for an immediate halt to Iranian attacks on countries across the region and urged that diplomacy be given a chance. Qatar also condemned the attacks on Bahrain, warning that their continuation marked a serious escalation that undermined efforts to ease tensions.

The Guards, meanwhile, issued a further warning to Bahrain.

Spokesman Hossein Mohebbi accused its government of cooperating in attacks on Iran and relying on a US “security bubble,” saying those policies would cast doubt on Bahrain’s survival in a new regional security order.
